2026-08-06T04:12:50.7347517Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7347894Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7348224Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7348704Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7349113Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7349607Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7351459Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7353189Z >
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7355477Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7357851Z >
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7358648Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7359391Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7359577Z ### How to Use
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7359815Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7360508Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7361386Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7361582Z ```bash
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7362166Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7362900Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7363872Z ```
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7364090Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7364390Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7364947Z ```bash
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7365503Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7366845Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7367751Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7368496Z ```
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7368704Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7369360Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7370336Z ```bash
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7370958Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7371848Z ```
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7372056Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7372599Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7373200Z ```bash
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7373741Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7374612Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7375311Z ```
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7375511Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7375790Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7376201Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7377615Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7379163Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7379343Z ```bash
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7380620Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7382105Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7382953Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7383258Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7383774Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7385242Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7386065Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7386547Z ```
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7386743Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7387509Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7388401Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7388578Z ```bash
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7389639Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7390682Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7391602Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7392409Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7392843Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7393649Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7394199Z ```
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7394400Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7394622Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7395456Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7396430Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7397405Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7398754Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7399904Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7400440Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7400625Z ### Notes
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7401360Z 
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7402036Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7403492Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7404759Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7406005Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7407207Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7408440Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7409407Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7410096Z </mcp-clis>

2026-08-06T04:12:50.7424688Z Create a daily digest workflow for professional developers, referencing
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7425571Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7426755Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7427682Z Hacker News API (https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/topstories.json),
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7428547Z filter to stories with a score above 100 that are about software
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7429348Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7430198Z distributed systems. For each qualifying story include: the title, the

2026-08-06T04:12:50.7432064Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
2026-08-06T04:12:50.7432968Z titled "HN Digest – <date>" with the results formatted as a Markdown
